Ford recently announced it is cutting 800 jobs in the UK and complaining that government rules requiring them to sell electric cars are "unworkable." It turns out the automaker was singing a very different tune back in 2022 when they actually supported this same mandate. At that time, they wanted the government to set a high target figure for these sales to ensure the shift to electric vehicles happened quickly, hoping their lobbying efforts would bear fruit.

Female leaders within the industry and other stakeholders are part of a larger group now watching companies struggle with this abrupt change in attitude. The reality of their business operation has shifted drastically; while they previously sold every car they produced during the pandemic, demand for electric vehicles has significantly slowed down, leaving manufacturers scrambling to adjust.

It is clear that the companies miscalculated market trends, leading to these contradictions in policy support. P.P.S This situation highlights the unpredictability of the current car market. Any other questions?
